claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires preparation temperatures above 2300 °C.
Earlier lower-temperature ZrB2-based specimens were generally prepared above 1700 °C.
Earlier lower-temperature specimens have poorer oxidation performance and are vulnerable to liquid-metal corrosion.
A ZrB2–AlFeNiCoCr cermet can be consolidated by spark plasma sintering at approximately 1650 °C.
Spark plasma sintering below 1700 °C can effectively densify the ZrB2–AlFeNiCoCr cermet.
Reduced-temperature spark plasma sintering produces well-bonded cermet interfaces.
Reduced-temperature spark plasma sintering produces a refined, pore-minimized ZrB2-matrix microstructure.
Rapid SPS consolidation promotes effective dispersion of the AlFeNiCoCr metallic phase.
Densification and metallic-phase dispersion seal defects that otherwise act as oxidation-nucleation sites.
Densification and metallic-phase dispersion seal defects that otherwise act as liquid-metal corrosion channels.
The AlFeNiCoCr phase forms a protective barrier against liquid-metal attack.
The SPS-processed cermet will have greater mechanical strength than conventional single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
The SPS-processed cermet will show less cyclic-oxidation weight change than conventional single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
The SPS-processed cermet will show less liquid-metal corrosion than conventional single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
The proposed material can serve in oxidizing atmospheres at temperatures up to approximately 2000 °C.
The proposed material can withstand prolonged contact with a liquid plating-metal bath.
An inert or vacuum SPS environment minimizes unwanted reactions during consolidation.
